terms.comment: Pliny’s and Quintilian’s verb in this sense (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Liv. 1.39.2: dōnec suā sponte experrēctus esset

phrases.latin: ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam, saepe ante, tardius rārō
phrases.english: I wake up when I like, usually about the first hour, often before, seldom later

phrases.latin: sī dormīs expergīscere, sī stās ingredere, sī ingrederis curre, sī curris advolā
phrases.english: if you’re asleep, wake up; if you’re standing, walk; if you’re walking, run; if you’re running, fly

phrases.latin: cum somnō repetītō simul cum sōle experrēctus essem
phrases.english: when I had gone back to sleep and woken with the sun

phrases.latin: movērī vetuisse puerum dōnec suā sponte experrēctus esset
phrases.english: she forbade anyone to move the boy until he woke up of his own accord

sources: Lewis & Short: evigilo · Lewis & Short: expergiscor
